pattern: WAI-ARIA APG Dialog (Modal) pattern implemented with native <dialog>.showModal(); non-modal sheets use <dialog>.show(). With two or more snap points the drag handle follows the APG Slider pattern.

aria.value: Implicit true for modal sheets (native showModal()); absent for non-modal sheets
Lowest / highest snap point as a whole percent of the viewport height
Current snap point as a whole percent

keyboard.action: Moves focus among sheet controls (close button, handle slider, content); the background is inert.
Follows document order; focus can leave the sheet and reach the page.

keyboard.context: Sheet is the topmost overlay, closeOnEscape=true
keyboard.action: Emits cancelable aui-cancel (reason 'escape'), then closes and restores focus.
No effect; the native close request is prevented, including repeated presses.
Cancels the drag only; the sheet returns to its height and stays open.
Next larger snap point (stops at the largest); emits aui-snap-change.
Next smaller snap point (stops at the smallest); emits aui-snap-change. Never closes the sheet.

keyboard.context: Close button or content button focused

focus: On open, focus moves to the first focusable element (native dialog focusing steps): the close button when shown, since it precedes the handle in DOM order. A non-modal sheet with no focusable content focuses the dialog itself (tabindex -1). On close, a modal sheet returns focus to the element focused before opening; a non-modal sheet does so only when focus was inside the sheet or on the body. Hiding the focused close button through configuration moves focus to the dialog.
notes: Dragging is never the only way to operate the sheet (WCAG 2.5.7): with two or more snap points a single click on the handle cycles the heights and the handle is keyboard-operable; dismissal is also available through Escape and the close button.
The handle strip spans the full width at control-height-sm height, a large touch target (WCAG 2.5.8).
Background inertness and top-layer rendering of modal sheets are provided by the browser.
Slide motion is removed under prefers-reduced-motion and data-aui-animation='none'.
The handle is shown first visually but follows the header in DOM and focus order.
knownCaveats: Manual screen-reader verification (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver) is pending.
Snap changes are conveyed through the slider's aria-valuetext only; there is no separate live-region announcement.
When closeOnEscape, showCloseButton, and closeOnDragDown are all false, the sheet has no built-in dismissal; the consumer must provide one.
